newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila stocks wallow in misery, "bye to bulls?".
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila stocks wallow in misery, "bye to bulls?".

text.p: Philippine stocks, haunted by the spectre of another U.S. interest rate increase and gloom at Wall Street, plunged to its year low on Friday and the bearish mood is likely to persist for weeks, analysts said.

Apparently reflecting the market's dim outlook, a power failure stopped trading but restoration of the lights more than an hour later failed to halt the fall of the main index, which dropped to its lowest level in nearly five months.
The index closed closed 44.18 points down, or 1.42 percent, at 3,060.59, the lowest since November 11 last year when the market's main barometer skidded to 3,046.97.
Value turnover was substantial at 2.3 billion pesos considering the temporary stoppage of trading.
"It's going to be a market dictated by Wall Street and by the U.S. Fed for the rest of the year," said Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
"Personally, I can say, bye-bye to the bullish market for the rest of the year," Reyes said, adding there could be brief rallies in between.
"It's going to be a non-trending market, the kind that's going to jerk you around, carry you to 3,200 and bring you back to below 3000."
Analyst Vangie Yap of Abacus Securities Corp said she foresaw the bearish sentiment to persist at least for the next two weeks.

This would be mainly due to apprehensions about an expected hike in the U.S. interest rate. She said expected release of first quarter corporate earnings in the next few weeks was unlikely to energise the market.

"Sentiment on a rate hike again and concern on funds flow would seem to overshadow positive earning results so what we're hoping is the market will correct to a certain level so that it will be attractive for people to reenter," Yap said.
"I think a lot of people have a pretty good level of cash. It's just that they're waiting for better prices."
Among the biggest losers was San Miguel Corp B shares which dropped nine pesos, or 10 percent, to 81 pesos. San Miguel A, on the other hand, ended steady at 55 pesos.

"Some people are raising questions on the deal between San Miguel and Coca-Cola Amatil but since other B shares are down and San Miguel A shares ended unchanged, then it's a combination of both the bearishness of the market and concerns on the deal," said Raymond Garcia, president at Diversified Securities.
